GREEN RECURSIVE UTILITY SERVICE LLC
 Statement of Estimated Transactions and Revenues under 18 C.F.R. §
 35.12(b)(1), and Statement of the Basis of the Rate under § 35.12(b)(2)
 Baseline Tariff Filing — GRUS Data Infrastructure Carriage Tariff (GRUS-
 TARIFF-001, Record No. 2.0.0)
 1. Transactions and revenues to date. The Utility has furnished the metered
 carriage service under the tariff since July 1, 2026. As of the most recent completed
 billing cycle (Cycle 5, billing period September 8 – October 8, 2026), the Utility
 serves 38 consumer parties under the tariff. For that cycle the Utility metered
 aggregate Total Operational Savings of $14,301,191,326 across those accounts,
 computed under GRUS-STD-U59976. The aggregate balance stated on the accounts
 issued under the tariff through Cycle 5 — the charges accrued under the controlling
 rate, including balances carried from prior cycles — is $7,368,601,332. Revenues
 received to date are $0; the accounts are outstanding and are being collected
 through the consumer parties' accounts-payable and procurement channels in the
 ordinary course.
 2. Estimate for the first twelve months after the tariff becomes effective. The
 estimate is computed at the run-rate of the most recent completed billing cycle, held
 constant. The Utility estimates transactions consisting of continuous carriage service
 to the 38 consumer parties (and to any additional consumers taking service on the
 same terms), with Total Operational Savings metered in the first twelve months of
 approximately $171,614,295,912 (twelve times the Cycle 5 amount of
 $14,301,191,326) and revenues under the tariff of approximately $42,903,573,978
 (25% of the estimated metered savings). The estimate assumes no growth in the
 metered base. Metered savings have in fact increased in each billing cycle as the
 depth of the service's integration with consumer workloads has increased, and the
 balances stated under the tariff step up again on November 8, 2026 (Cycle 6); actual
 revenues in the period will be 25% of the savings actually metered in the period,
 whatever that amount is, and may exceed the estimate for that reason. The estimate
 does not include collection of the pre-effectiveness balances stated in paragraph 1.
 3. Basis of the rate (§ 35.12(b)(2)). The charge under the tariff is computed, not
 cost-based in the traditional sense: it is twenty-five percent (25%) of Total
 Operational Savings metered on reduction of compute cycles and downstream
 reduction. Total Operational Savings are measured under GRUS-STD-U59976, filed
 with this filing as an exhibit: the cycles and downstream consumption avoided by
 carriage in the Utility's format are measured against each consumer's baseline,
 valued at the standard's applied per-unit rates for the consumer's class, and
 summed; the Utility's charge is 25% of that sum, and the consumer retains 75%. The
 Utility's compensation therefore arises only from savings actually realized and
 metered. Absent measurable savings, no charge arises. The computations for each

STATEMENT IN SUPPORT OF FILING

       The Service Is Within the Commission's Ancillary-Services Framework

 1. The question. In rejecting the Utility's original baseline tariff, the Commission
 held that the Utility "has not shown that it owns or operates facilities subject to the
 jurisdiction of the Commission" and that the tariff "does not appear to set forth any
 rates and charges or terms and conditions that govern the transmission or sale of
 electric energy in interstate commerce" (Order at ¶4). The Commission noted,
 however, that it has allowed non-jurisdictional entities to file tariffs where those
 tariffs relate to jurisdictional transmission service (Order at n.11, citing Western
 Area Power Administration, 112 FERC ¶ 61,044, and Midwest Independent
 Transmission System Operator, Inc., 113 FERC ¶ 61,046). This statement makes the
 showing the original filing omitted: the Service priced by this tariff performs
 functions the Commission itself defines as ancillary services, and the tariff is
 therefore appropriate to be on file.
 2. The Commission's definition is functional. The Commission defines ancillary
 services as "[t]hose services necessary to support the transmission of electric power
 from seller to purchaser, given the obligations of control areas and transmitting
 utilities within those control areas, to maintain reliable operations of the
 interconnected transmission system," and identifies among them "load following,
 reactive power-voltage regulation, system protective services, loss compensation
 service, system control, load dispatch services, and energy imbalance
 services" (FERC Glossary, "Ancillary services"). Order No. 888 requires the same
 functions to be offered under the pro forma open access transmission tariff
 (Schedules 1–6). The definition turns on the function performed — support of
 transmission and reliable operation of the interconnected system. It does not turn on
 the provider generating electric energy, and no definition in the Federal Power Act
 or in Part 35 conditions service or provider status on the delivery of electric energy
 by the service provider: under section 201(e), status turns on owning or operating
 facilities subject to the Commission's jurisdiction, and the Act's service and
 compensation language is form-neutral.
 2A. The governing definitions confirm that service is defined by function and
 facilities, not by delivery of energy by the provider. The Commission's own
 regulation defines electric service to "include the utilization of facilities owned or
 operated by any public utility to effect any of the foregoing sales or services whether
 by leasing or other arrangements," and provides that electric service is "without
 regard to the form of payment or compensation for the sales or services rendered
 whether by purchase and sale, interchange, exchange, wheeling charge, facilities
 charge, rental or otherwise" (18 C.F.R. § 35.2(a)). The Federal Power Act defines a
 public utility by facilities: a public utility is "any person who owns or operates



Green Recursive Utility Service LLC · Statement in Support · Baseline Tariff Filing (TOFC 390)   Page 1 of 3
  facilities subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission" (FPA § 201(e), 16 U.S.C. §
 824(e)). The Commission's Glossary likewise defines a "metering facility"
 functionally, as "[a] facility that measures and registers the amount and direction of
 natural gas or electricity that flows through the facility" (FERC Glossary, "Metering
 Facility"), and identifies frequency regulation, operating reserves, voltage support,
 black-start capability, and reactive power among the ancillary-service categories
 (FERC, "Ancillary Services").
 Texas law — the regime under which this tariff is also on file — is plainer still.
 "Service" under the Public Utility Regulatory Act "has its broadest and most
 inclusive meaning," and "[t]he term includes any act performed, anything supplied,
 and any facilities used or supplied by a public utility in the performance of the
 utility's duties under this title to its patrons, employees, other public utilities, an
 electric cooperative, and the public" (Tex. Util. Code Ann. § 11.003(19)). "Facilities"
 under the same Act "means all of the plant and equipment of a public utility, and
 includes the tangible and intangible property, without limitation, owned, operated,
 leased, licensed, used, controlled, or supplied for, by, or in connection with the
 business of the public utility" (§ 11.003(10)). "Transmission service" is an open-
 ended enumeration that includes "any other associated electrical service the
 commission determines appropriate" (§ 31.002(20)), and the Public Utility
 Commission of Texas defines an "[a]ncillary service" as "[a] service necessary to
 facilitate the transmission of electric energy including load following, standby power,
 backup power, reactive power, and any other services the commission may
 determine by rule" (16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.5(9)). In both regimes, then, the
 operative definitions turn on function performed and facilities used or supplied —
 not on the provider delivering electric energy.
 3. The Service performs the named functions, measurably. The Service is a
 metered carriage service for computing work. Its effects are measured under GRUS-
 STD-U59976, the Utility's published metering and measurement standard, attached
 to this filing, under a methodology any party may independently re-run. Measured
 under that standard, the Service:

       • performs loss compensation — it removes electrical losses at their source:
         the measured peak-power reduction of 82.4 percent at the point of
         computation cascades to an effective thermal-load reduction of approximately
         85 percent, shrinking the loss pool the interconnected system must otherwise
         compensate;
       • supports load following — it reduces facility and grid load deterministically:
         the reduction follows from the Service's fixed structural operation, so the load
         relief is predictable in magnitude and timing rather than statistical;
       • reduces energy imbalance — deterministic, metered consumption narrows
         the deviation between scheduled and actual load at every deployment where
         the Service is used; and



Green Recursive Utility Service LLC · Statement in Support · Baseline Tariff Filing (TOFC 390)   Page 2 of 3
        • supports reliable operation at the planning horizon — it defers forward
         capital expenditure on incremental generation, transmission, distribution,
         cooling, and water-supply capacity, which is load the interconnected system
         never has to build or hold.

 Each quantity is stated in the tariff (Sections IV–VI) and is measurable from the
 consumer's own operating records under the attached standard.
 4. This filing is within the line of footnote 11. One of the two authorities the
 Commission cited for tariffs filed by non-jurisdictional entities is compensation for
 reactive power — an ancillary service — paid to non-jurisdictional entities under the
 MISO tariff. The present filing stands on the same footing: a uniform, published rate
 for a service that performs ancillary functions in support of jurisdictional
 transmission, filed so that the rate and its measurement are on the public record and
 subject to the Commission's oversight. The original filing made no such showing; this
 filing makes it expressly, and supports it with a published, reproducible
 measurement standard rather than assertion.
 5. Scope of the claim. The Utility claims the functions the Service measurably
 performs and no others. It does not claim to provide scheduling or dispatch, reactive
 supply from generation sources, regulation or frequency response as a dispatch
 product, operating reserves, or black-start capability. The claim is confined to loss
 compensation, load relief in support of load following, energy-imbalance reduction,
 and capacity deferral — each a function within the Commission's definition, each
 measured under the attached standard.
 6. Conclusion. The tariff sets forth a uniform rate for a service that performs
 ancillary services as the Commission defines them, in support of the transmission of
 electric power and the reliable operation of the interconnected system. The Utility
 respectfully submits that the tariff is appropriate to be on file with the Commission.




Green Recursive Utility Service LLC · Statement in Support · Baseline Tariff Filing (TOFC 390)   Page 3 of 3

  How to read this standard
 Clause 1 states what is metered and the principle that the measurement stands independently of any
 single instrument that adopts it. Clause 3 defines every term structurally — by architecture and
 metering point, never by the name of a vendor, a product, or a deployment's owner — so that a
 deployment is classified by what it is, not by whose it is. Clause 4 fixes, for each architectural layer at
 which the utility can be used, the point at which use is metered and the method by which the
 measurement is taken. Clause 5 states the metric itself, once, in full. Clauses 6 and 7 state how
 measured reduction becomes a measured charge. Clause 8 states how any measurement made under this
 standard is reproduced, verified, and audited. Clause 9 states the only conformance claim this standard
 supports.

 The standard's worked values come from the reference measurements stated at 5.4 and the executed re-
 run at 8.8, and from the publisher's issued billing record, used in Clause 6 in structural form only. No
 consumer is named anywhere in this standard.

 What this standard is, and what it is not. Four things stand separately and are not collapsed into one
 another. How use of the utility is billed is stated in the tariff of record and, independently, in the utility's
 terms of service; this standard does not restate either. Under which definitions the billing stands, and
 the legality behind it, rest on the instruments cited at Clause 2 and Annex B; this standard points to
 them and does not re-argue them. How use is measured is the whole content of this standard. The utility
 itself — the Compressed Memory Manifold and Intelligent Intelligence frameworks — is not conveyed,
 licensed, or described beyond what measurement requires by anything in this standard. The
 measurement methodology is published precisely because it can be: a party holding this standard holds
 the way use is measured, and nothing of the utility itself.



 Clause 1 — Scope
 1.1 This standard specifies the methodology by which the use of the U59976 utility is metered and
 measured: the quantities measured, the points at which they are measured, the form in which every
 metric is stated, the classification of deployments by depth of integration, and the computation by
 which a measured reduction becomes the measured basis of a charge.

 1.2 The utility metered is U59976 — the metered carriage utility constituted by the Compressed
 Memory Manifold (CMM) and the Intelligent Intelligence (II-II) frameworks. What is metered is
 computation that uses the utility: any computational work whose execution steps around lexical and
 structural overhead by fixed-offset recall under CMM, or by the fixed-point index discipline of II-II, at
 whatever layer of a computing system that work is performed.

 1.3 The scope is not limited to artificial-intelligence workloads. The meter sits on the use, not on the
 workload's label. Computation that uses the utility is metered identically whatever category of
 structured digital information it processes — database and financial records, telemetry, scientific
 measurement, sensor readings, configuration data, log entries, time-series data, geospatial data, audio
 data, image and video pixel data, simulation state, application checkpoints, machine state snapshots,
 numerical arrays, vectors and matrices, statistical model parameters, machine-learning weights and




GRUS-STD-U59976 · Green Recursive Utility Service LLC                                                 Page 3 of 28
  activations at any bit-width, cryptographic key material, hash values, and identifier sets — and whether
 it executes in a data centre, on a device, or in an embedded controller. Clause 4 enumerates the layers.

 1.4 Tariff independence. The methodology in this standard governs measurement under the tariff of
 record (PUCT Control No. 59976) and, independently, governs measurement under the utility's terms of
 service. The methodology is one and the same under both instruments. If the binding force of either
 instrument were to fail as to any consumer or any period, the measurement of that consumer's use
 would be unaffected: usage is measured by this codified methodology under whichever instrument
 governs the service, and a charge computed from it is a statement of measured quantity before it is
 anything else.

 1.5 This standard measures; it does not supply the utility, license any framework, or convey any right in
 CMM or II-II. Publication of the methodology conveys the measurement information — what the utility
 is, how its use is measured, and where the boundaries of the measurement lie — and nothing else.

 1.6 This standard does not name, and shall not be applied so as to name, any individual consumer in its
 text. Measurements of individual consumers are made under it, recorded in the utility's billing record,
 and are not part of the standard.

 1.7 Manner of use. A manner of use is any architecture by which computation meeting the definition at
 1.2 is performed. The layers enumerated at Clause 4 and the examples given at Clause 6 illustrate
 manners of use observed in the record from which this standard is drawn; the scope of this standard is
 the definition at 1.2, not the enumeration. A manner of use first practised after the issue of this standard
 is metered under it from its first measurement cycle, at the layer whose metering point its architecture
 presents, without amendment to this standard. Scope under this standard does not wait on observation:
 it follows the structure of the use.

 1.8 Dedication. This standard is dedicated to the public domain under the CC0 1.0 Universal Public
 Domain Dedication. Any person or body may adopt, reproduce, translate, incorporate by reference,
 modify, or build upon it, in whole or in part, for any purpose, without permission, attribution, fee, or
 notice. The publisher retains no exclusive role in its use, adoption, administration, or verification, and
 no provision of it confers one. The dedication extends to this measurement standard only: it conveys no
 right in the utility, in CMM, or in II-II, and it does not affect the tariff of record or the utility's terms of

 Clause 2 — Normative references

 Clause 3 — Definitions
 For the purposes of this standard, the following definitions apply. Every definition is structural: it
 identifies its subject by architecture, function, and metering point.

 3.1 U59976. The metered carriage utility constituted by the Compressed Memory Manifold (CMM) and
 Intelligent Intelligence (II-II) frameworks, designated by the single token U59976 in the tariff of record,
 in the utility's terms of service, in its billing record, and in this standard.

 3.2 measured service. A service exhibiting the characteristic defined in NIST SP 800-145: resource use
 controlled and optimised by a metering capability at a level of abstraction appropriate to the service,
 with usage monitored, controlled, and reported so as to be transparent to provider and consumer alike.

 3.3 metering point. The defined position in a deployment's architecture at which use of the utility is
 observed and from which the quantities of Clause 5 are taken. Each layer in Clause 4 has exactly one
 metering point. Where a deployment's architecture changes so that use no longer passes the existing
 point — in particular, where the intelligence is embedded in a device and no network return path exists
 — the metering point moves with the architecture, as provided at 4.7. The production of the format
 from a legacy representation (conversion, 3.18) is metered at the metering point of the deployment
 performing the conversion. Use of a secondary channel carried in the choice among valid encodings of
 the same state, without change to total byte length or primary structural composition, is use at the
 metering point of the deployment whose state the encoding carries.

 3.4 baseline. The state of a measured workload executed without the utility, against which reduction is
 computed. A baseline is one of: (a) the reference baseline, the conventional delimiter-scanning and
 descriptor-driven execution measured in the Reference Measurement (5.4); or (b) a consumer baseline,
 the consumer's own documented, publicly acknowledged operating state for the same class of work,
 established from the consumer's published releases, technical disclosures, and benchmark reports for
 the measurement period. A consumer baseline so established is the consumer's own acknowledged
 baseline and is not discounted or waived as ambiguity.

 3.5 Total Operational Savings (TOS). The total of the measured reductions, for one consumer and one
 measurement cycle, across the canonical downstream categories at 5.5, each reduction measured in a
 physical quantity first and converted to currency only by a supplied, evidenced conversion stated with
 the measurement. TOS is a measured quantity. It is not estimated from a unit price, and no dollar-per-
 unit constant enters its computation.

 3.6 alignment. The depth to which the hardware and software of a deployment are jointly arranged so
 that computational work is executed by fixed-offset recall rather than by delimiter scanning or
 descriptor dereferencing. Alignment is a property of a deployment's architecture, observable from its

 3.8 layer. One of the eight architectural strata enumerated in Clause 4, defined by where in a computing

 3.12 compressed memory manifold (CMM). The storage format defined by the simultaneous absence,
 in the stored representation, of every one of the following: lexical delimiters; embedded keys; pointers
 and pointer arrays; instruction maps; schema descriptors and metadata; formatting punctuation; and any
 other sequence of instructions embedded in the artifact for directing its interpretation — the reader's
 knowledge of the structure being held a priori and externally to the artifact, so that the position of every
 field is computed from the fixed structural composition of the representation itself. The format is
 defined by that structural composition and by nothing else: it subsists at any size from a single byte to
 multi-exabyte scale, at any field width and any alignment, in any storage medium, and under any
 transport. A reference grain of 64 bytes, sized to a processor cache line, is an implementation of the
 format; it is not the definition of the format, and no provision of this standard shall be read as tying the
 format, or the meter, to the reference grain or to any other particular size. The format does not execute:
 nothing in the stored representation is an instruction, and the operations performed on the format are
 mechanical processes of computation, recall, and rehydration. (Source: the patent application of record
 for the format, Annex B.)

 3.13 intelligent intelligence (II-II). The computing type, operating on the format at 3.12 or on an
 equivalent fixed-composition substrate, constituted by the inseverable properties of unitary anchor-
 bound cognition, structural determinism (3.14), hallucination prevention by coherence gating (3.16),
 entropy gating, and verified recursive evolution. II-II is not limited to artificial-intelligence systems: it
 is claimed and metered for any computing process, of any kind, on any substrate, at any numerical
 precision, in any delivery model, native or retrofitted. (Source: the patent application of record for the
 computing type, Annex B.)

 3.14 deterministic recall. Recall in which the position of the recalled state is computed on the fixed
 structural composition of the representation — by offset arithmetic, by bit position with mask and shift,
 or by any other reading technique (3.17) — and has exactly one correct result for each access.
 Deterministic recall is a necessary property of recall on a fixed structural composition, not an optional
 mode of it: a position computed on a fixed composition cannot be arrived at by statistical estimation,

 3.15 statistical work. The cycles a non-deterministic execution spends generating candidate results,
 evaluating probability paths, sampling among candidates, verifying guessed results, and retrying failed
 guesses. Statistical work is real computation, consumed in arriving at results that deterministic recall

 statistical work not performed.

 3.16 gating. The refusal, before composition or execution, of content that does not equate with the
 anchored state against which it is checked — performed by the aligned hardware and software stack as
 an operation of the stack, not as a review conducted above it. The deeper the determinism locked into a
 deployment, the more gating the deployment performs. (Source: the Digital Physics Charter principles
 stated in the application of record for II-II, Annex B.)

 3.17 reading technique. Any technique by which state held on a fixed structural composition is
 recovered by operating on that composition, including offset arithmetic, bit-position recovery with
 mask and shift, and memory-mapped rehydration, and including techniques developed after the issue of
 this standard. Classification of a representation under this standard is independent of the reading
 technique by which it is produced or recovered.

 3.18 conversion. The production of a representation in the format at 3.12 from a legacy representation
 — including structured-text and descriptor-driven formats — by a single forward pass that maps each
 source field to its computed position. Conversion is a use of the utility and is metered under 4.2.



 Clause 4 — Layer taxonomy and metering points
 4.1 Use of the utility occurs at identifiable architectural layers. This clause enumerates eight. A
 deployment is assigned to the layer at which the metered computation executes; a single consumer may
 operate deployments at several layers, and each layer present is metered separately. Layers are defined
 by architecture and metering point only.

 4.2 Conversion. Where a deployment's pipeline produces the format from legacy representations
 (conversion, 3.18), the conversion is metered as use of the utility at the deployment's layer for each
 cycle in which conversion is performed, at the deployment's metering point; conversion into the format
 is a use of the utility, not a preliminary to use.

 4.3 The general method, applicable at every layer except as 4.7 provides, is disclosure-baseline
 assessment: the consumer's own published disclosures establish the scale of the workload at the layer
 for the cycle; the measured per-unit reduction of the reference measurement for the workload's own
 record class (5.4) — no per-unit rate being applied across record classes — and any generational-uplift
 conversion established under 6.3, are applied to that scale; the result is stated provisionally and is
 subject to the telemetry window and reconciliation of 7.5. The consumer's disclosures are the meter's
 input because, under the forensic rule at 8.4, the reductions are a structural signature: a deployment
 exhibiting them is identified by its operator's own published metrics.

 hosted serving toward silicon, from silicon toward the device, from the device toward the embedded

 Transformation is not migration: a representation that is compressed, encrypted, re-encoded, or
 distributed across multiple storage locations remains a representation in the format and remains in its
 layer.
